items.title: Research spike: cross-list sanctions screening next to gankdat's uk-sanctions — OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN exports (Sanctions List Service: export names, SDN.CSV layout, advanced XML, update cadence), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list's access route and terms, two paid rivals' per-query prices (OpenSanctions screening credits and reseller licence, sanctions.io or ComplyAdvantage) and gankdat's uk-sanctions external calls; write docs/exchange/spikes/ofac-eu-sanctions-screening.md with a promote / park call
items.why: Exchange pre-research 2026-10-18 (burn-down, relay sanctions-lists-2026-10-18, the first pass under the spike rule): SDN.CSV answers HEAD 200 text/csv, last-modified 2026-10-15 16:34 UTC, and its first 4 kB are `ent_num,name,type,program,…` rows with `-0-` placeholders (a flat per-entry CSV, simpler than the UK list's per-name CSV); `CONS_ADVANCED.XML` answered 400, so the export names must be read from the service page first; ofac.treasury.gov/sanctions-list-service is 200 with the Advanced Sanctions Data Model documentation (a US government work — public domain, no licence step); opensanctions.org/licensing confirms the paid shape — hosted screening billed per query through prepaid credit bundles plus a wholesale reseller licence for redistribution — but shows no figure on that page; sanctions.io/pricing is 404 (moved); the data.europa.eu dataset slug guessed for the EU list is 404. Why it is worth a spike and not a parked idea: a screening call is a per-query cut of money already flowing (KYC/KYB checks every payments, invoicing and marketplace product runs), gankdat already streams the UK list (uk-sanctions: 162 calls in 30 d, 0 external) so the ingest pattern and the Blind Mode minimisation exist, and the open question is a number — do rivals charge enough per query for a three-list `screen_name` tool to clear x402's floor, and does any external caller use the UK list at all. Park if no rival sells cross-list screening above US$0.01 a query or the EU list needs an account. — Spike 2026-10-18 (docs/exchange/spikes/ofac-eu-sanctions-screening.md): parked. Supply is clean (OFAC exports public domain, EU FSF reachable with the Commission's public token, no account), rivals charge €0.03–0.10 a query hosted and US$0.002–0.08 on Apify, but uk-sanctions has 0 external calls in 30 d and the 17 Apify screening actors share ~20 monthly users; re-open on the first external uk-sanctions/sam-exclusions call or a screening request.
items.proof: the spike file states the three lists' access terms and update cadence, the real OFAC export names, two rival per-query prices and gankdat's uk-sanctions external-call count, with a promote / park recommendation the 2026-10-21 exchange cites

items.title: Research spike: Beefy harvest call fees on Base — relay-read Beefy's fee documentation (the caller's share of the performance fee, per chain) and api.beefy.finance's vault, fee and TVL lists for Base, then a week of StratHarvest(harvester, wantHarvested, tvl) logs on Base through the Tenderly keyless RPC (the keeper spike's proven path) with wantHarvested priced; count the call-fee value reaching harvesters outside the top address; write docs/exchange/spikes/beefy-harvest-call-fees.md with a promote / park call (≥ US$20 a week outside the top address promotes a Worker-only harvester with no capital and no contract; below it the keeper idea is declined outright)
items.why: The 2026-10-17 keeper spike declined liquidations (US$160k in 7 days to 61 bots, 85–93 % to the top five, repayment capital needed) and kept one trigger: harvest call fees, a measurement nobody has run. WebSearch 2026-10-19: Beefy's Strategy Contract docs (developer documentation, last updated 2023) say every harvest() call charges fees paid to the harvest caller, the strategist and the treasury; a third-party contract mirror splits the 4.5 % performance fee as 3 % BIFI stakers, 0.5 % treasury, 0.5 % strategist, 0.5 % harvest caller (Ethereum mainnet figure — the Base share and the current docs are the relay read; docs.beefy.finance does not resolve from the sandbox). The question is contention, not design: Beefy runs its own harvester bot, so the number is what, if anything, reaches other callers in a week. Hosts docs.beefy.finance and api.beefy.finance added to docs/relay/hosts.txt tonight; base.gateway.tenderly.co is already allowed (≤ 1,000 blocks a call, one call per line). — Spike 2026-10-19 (docs/exchange/spikes/beefy-harvest-call-fees.md): declined. Beefy's /fees API sets the harvest caller's share at 0.01 % of yield on all 537 Base vaults (docs say 0.05–0.5 %); the 226 active vaults hold US$14.98 M earning ≈ US$52,011 a week at listed APY, so the whole chain's call-fee pool is US$5.20 a week at 100 % capture; a 6.7-hour StratHarvest sample (477 events, 11 harvesters) gives 89 % to one bot and ≈ US$0.59 a week to everyone outside it, below Base gas per harvest. onchain-keeper-rewards declined in the exchange.
items.proof: the spike file holds the caller fee share on Base, 7-day harvest count, call-fee value by harvester address and the share outside the top address, with a promote / park call

items.title: Research spike: EU high-value-dataset company registers beyond Ireland — which member-state registers are published keyless under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/138 (bulk download, API, licence) for the five largest economies and the Nordics, read from data.europa.eu's company-ownership HVD category and the national portals; two paid rivals priced per lookup (OpenCorporates' self-serve tiers, one KYB vendor); Apify actors reselling EU company lookups and their monthly users; write docs/exchange/spikes/eu-hvd-company-registers.md sizing the one-feed sibling idea with a promote / park call
items.why: The 2026-10-13 Ireland CRO pre-research parked the Irish register (score 2, gated on uk-companies converting) and asked the exchange to size the sibling: one EU company feed from every register the HVD regulation obliges member states to publish free of charge with bulk and API (company ownership is one of its six categories, in force since 2024). WebSearch 2026-10-19 confirms the obligation and one live example (Ireland: CC BY 4.0, daily, bulk + API) but no country-by-country status page — that count is the spike. Rival price read tonight: OpenCorporates' self-serve API is £2,250 a year for 500 calls a month up to £12,000 a year for 5,000 (≈ £0.24–4.50 a call at the cap, no self-serve free tier on the official page), which leaves room for a per-call x402/MCP lookup if ≥ 3 registers are keyless under an open licence; park if the registers are behind national accounts or share-alike terms, or if the EU company actors on Apify show < 10 users each. — Spike 2026-10-19 (docs/exchange/spikes/eu-hvd-company-registers.md): parked. Supply clears the bar — data.europa.eu tags 119 company-category HVDs in 13 countries, eight of them national registers, and seven registers answered keyless under an open licence (Ireland CC BY, France Licence Ouverte with a 7-calls/s search API, Finland CC BY API, Poland's KRS extract API, Latvia's 129 MB daily CSV, Sweden's 251 MB weekly bulk zip, Malta's API) — but Germany, Italy and Spain publish no register (5 / 0 / 23 tagged datasets, none the register; Handelsregister's terms cap 60 queries an hour), the Netherlands' file strips names and KvK numbers, Denmark and Belgium need accounts, Luxembourg is CC BY-SA. Rivals: OpenCorporates £2,250–12,000 a year (£0.20–0.38 a call at the caps), Know Your Customer US$19–119 a record, CompanyData credits from US$34 a month, Apify multi-register actors US$0.002–0.01 a record. Demand: 114 European-register Apify actors share 483 users/30 d; the 13 with ≥ 10 users all scrape closed registers (Handelsregister 219 users across 30 actors, North Data 125, Registro Mercantil 44, KvK 36, Registro Imprese 18); the open registers draw 1–4 users per actor (France 11 across 7; Ireland 1; Poland 3; Finland ≤ 2); gankdat uk-companies 161 calls/30 d, 0 external. Score ≈ 0.7. Re-open on a first paid company call, an EU register request, or a de/it/es national register appearing in the HVD facet; France (Sirene + recherche-entreprises, ≈ 1 day) first if it does.
items.proof: the spike file lists ≥ 8 member states with access route, licence and update cadence, two rival per-lookup prices, the Apify actor user counts and a promote / park call

items.title: Research spike: US NPI provider registry (CMS NPPES, 8M+ healthcare providers) as a gankdat lookup — read the official API page and the Data Dissemination page through the relay (keyless, 200 records a call, 1,200 a query, monthly bulk file size and refresh, redistribution terms), the monthly users and prices of the ten NPI actors on the Apify Store, and one non-Apify paid rival per lookup; write docs/exchange/spikes/us-npi-registry.md with the users-to-price number and a promote / park call
items.why: Exchange pre-research 2026-10-19 17:25 (burn-down, WebSearch; the CMS and Apify hosts are not reachable from the sandbox, so the numbers below are secondhand and the spike reads the primary pages through the relay). Licence: the NPPES Data Dissemination Notice (72 FR 30011, 30 May 2007) made the FOIA-disclosable NPI data public from September 2007 as a downloadable file, monthly updates and a query-only registry at no charge; the 2024 and 2025 notices (89 FR, 4 March 2024; CMS-0063-N, 31 July 2025) change the published elements, not the access. API: NPPES API 2.1, GET, no key, JSON, at most 200 records a call and 1,200 a query; no rate limit stated (the R package docs); the full file is the NPI Downloadable File. Paid rivals on the shelf gankdat already sells on: at least ten NPI actors on the Apify Store priced US$2.80–8.00 per 1,000 results (benthepythondev 2.80, crawlergang 3.00 with a 5.0 rating from 11 reviews, crawlerbros 3.00, retrainmap 5.00, scrapers_lat 8.00 pay-per-event; haketa, logiover, opendata-labs, cblu, pink_comic, parseforge unpriced in the results), a 'health provider api' with a free tier of 100 lookups a month and PayerPrice's credit-metered /api/v1/npis — monthly users unread (the Apify stat the spike reads; the third-party radar shows logiover at 4.3× 7-day momentum and parseforge cooling). Fit: the shelf is one more keyless US register beside sam-exclusions (built, D1 with idOf) and the NHS ODS sibling; demand is US healthcare developers and billing teams, the biggest provider-lookup market, and the Apify prices put a ceiling of ≈ US$0.003–0.008 a record on what a per-call x402/MCP lookup can charge. Promote if the ten actors sum to ≥ 100 monthly users and the terms allow redistribution (FOIA data, expected); park if the bulk file's monthly refresh makes a cached D1 copy stale against a free daily-refreshed official API, or if the actors' users sit under 30 in total. Evidence 1.5 (rivals priced on our shelf, users unread) × reach 2 (Apify + MCP + x402, built listings) ÷ 0.5 days = 6. — Spike 2026-10-19 17:40 (docs/exchange/spikes/us-npi-registry.md): parked. CMS terms read from the primary page: FOIA-disclosed, query-only registry updated daily and a monthly 1,106 MB bulk file, both at no charge; the API answered keyless in under a second. The Apify Store API lists 71 NPI/NPPES actors sharing 114 users in 30 days (busiest 9, 45 at exactly 1), priced US$0.002–0.01 a record; the paid provider-data demand sits with scrapers of closed directories (Healthgrades, Zocdoc). Re-open on a sam-exclusions paid call, an NPI request, or an NPI + exclusion actor passing 10 users; the shape then is a live provider-verification call joining NPPES, sam-exclusions and the OIG LEIE, not a register copy.
items.proof: docs/exchange/spikes/us-npi-registry.md with the Apify users-to-price number, the API and file terms from the primary pages, and a promote / park call (a promote files the dataset item in the gankdat queue and the idea in the exchange)

items.title: Research spike: the Atlassian Marketplace as a paid shelf for a Forge app — relay-read the partner due-diligence page (registration number and/or tax ID: can a UK sole trader with a UTR verify as a paid-via-Atlassian partner?), the three 2026 community threads on individual vendors (97755, 101919, 102081 with the Partner team's 2026-08-10 reply), the pricing/payment FAQ (payout schedule, minimum, methods) and the Marketplace REST API 2 (keyless /rest/2/addons?hosting=cloud&cost=marketplace&application=confluence|jira with each app's /distribution totalInstalls and /pricing/cloud/live): count the paid cloud apps from small vendors with < 1,000 installs in a utility niche we could build in ≤ 1 week (macros, variables/tokens, lookups, exports), their per-user prices and the floor price; write docs/exchange/spikes/atlassian-marketplace-forge-shelf.md with a promote / park call
items.why: Exchange pre-research 2026-10-20 17:25 (burn-down, WebSearch; marketplace.atlassian.com and developer.atlassian.com do not resolve from the sandbox, so the spike reads them through the relay — four hosts added tonight). Why a shelf and not another register: every gankdat-sibling spike since 10-17 (NPI, OFAC/EU, EU registers, VAT) parked on the same fact — 0 external calls — while the operation's only product that has taken money sold through a shelf that supplies its own buyers and billing (Figma Community). The Atlassian Marketplace is that shape with billing attached: Atlassian sells the app as commercial agent, collects sales tax/VAT and pays the partner within 30 days of the month its profit passes US$500 (developer FAQ, pricing-payment-billing). Fee, read from Atlassian's 2026 revenue-share post and the FAQ: Forge-only apps carry a 0 % commission on revenue earned from 1 January 2026 until a partner's lifetime Forge revenue reaches US$1 million; the standard Forge rate otherwise is 16 % (17 % from 1 October 2026), Connect 20 %→25 %. Forge hosting is free (forge-free-pricing-2025). The open question is the one that decides it: three 2026 developer-community threads ask whether an individual without a registered company can sell — a March 2026 post says Partner Verification wants a registered business entity, an August 2026 post says a Portuguese sole trader was verified and listed paid-via-Atlassian, the due-diligence page asks for 'a registration number and/or tax identification number', and the Turkey thread holds a Partner-team reply dated 2026-08-10 the search cut off. Demand is the second number: the Marketplace REST API 2 is keyless and lists per-app installs and users (community tip 45128; three Apify actors resell it), so the spike can count the small-vendor paid apps in a buildable niche instead of guessing. Promote (open an atlassian-apps venture queue, owner action: partner registration with the UTR) if an individual/sole trader can verify and ≥ 3 paid cloud apps from vendors with one or two listings show ≥ 200 installs at ≥ US$1/user/month in a niche buildable in ≤ 1 week; park if verification needs a company (then the parked limited-company idea is the trigger) or no such niche shows. Score: evidence 1.5 (the shelf's billing and fee are read from Atlassian; the niche and eligibility are the spike) × reach 2 (300k+ Atlassian cloud customers, billing supplied) ÷ 0.5 days = 6. — Spike 2026-10-22 (docs/exchange/spikes/atlassian-marketplace-forge-shelf.md, build): eligibility met — a UK sole trader registers on the individual path (thread 101919, Partner-team document 2026-08-10; a Portuguese sole trader verified Paid via Atlassian 2026-09-01, the Identity form asks 'Are you a Sole Proprietor?'; Stripe Identity selfie + UTR + W-8BEN); payout EFT ≥ US$500 net, 30–60 days; fee 0 % to US$1M lifetime Forge revenue, 83 % after. Demand half not met as written: 4,477 paid cloud apps, seven small-vendor paid text-render macros with 202–911 installs, but priced US$0.10–0.69/user/month (the ≥ US$1 apps are workflow builds > 1 week); 10-user tier free on 20 of 25. Call: promote reshaped (a Forge-only Confluence text-render macro at US$0.40–0.50/user/month, ≈ 3 build days, owner verification as the queue's first blocked_on) — the 2026-10-28 exchange decides; recorded in the exchange as `atlassian-marketplace-forge-apps`.
items.proof: docs/exchange/spikes/atlassian-marketplace-forge-shelf.md states whether a UK sole trader can be a paid partner (quoting the due-diligence page and the Partner-team reply), the payout terms, ≥ 3 small-vendor paid apps in one niche with installs and per-user price from the REST API, and a promote / park call

items.title: Research spike: JetBrains Marketplace as a paid shelf — relay-read the current Developer Agreement and the Vendor Information help page (can a UK sole trader without a company register as a paid-plugin vendor? bank payout in USD/EUR within 30 days of month end, tax forms), the revenue-sharing page (15 % commission, cap 25 %, JetBrains handles VAT) and the keyless Marketplace search API (plugins.jetbrains.com/api/searchPlugins with pricingModels=PAID — downloads and rating per plugin; /api/plugins/{id} for the price): count paid plugins from vendors with ≤ 2 listings showing ≥ 2,000 downloads at ≥ US$10/user/year in a utility niche buildable in ≤ 1 week (formatters, data/regex/JSON tools, HTTP/API helpers, language-agnostic editor utilities); write docs/exchange/spikes/jetbrains-marketplace-paid-plugins.md with a promote / park call
items.why: new-ventures research 2026-10-22 (build; WebSearch — plugins.jetbrains.com and jetbrains.com do not resolve from the sandbox, hosts added for the relay). Why a second shelf after Atlassian: the 10-22 Atlassian spike passed every gate (sole trader eligible, billing supplied, 0 % fee) and failed only on unit price (US$0.10–0.69/user/month macros), so the next shelf to read is one with higher unit prices and the same buyer-and-billing supply. JetBrains Marketplace sells paid plugins as the merchant: its revenue-sharing help page sets the commission at 15 % of the sale price (changeable with one month's notice, never above 25 %; a reseller's cut comes out of JetBrains' share), taxes (VAT, withholding) are handled on top of the price, no listing or development fee; vendors are paid in USD or EUR to a bank account up to 30 days after month end under the Developer Agreement (v3.x: the vendor sets the list price and model — subscription or one-off — and plugins join JetBrains' educational and open-source discounts unless opted out). Open: whether the vendor account needs a legal entity (the help page speaks of the 'Vendor Information tab for your Organization'; no individual or sole-trader statement surfaced in search) and the niche numbers, which the API makes countable rather than guessed. VS Code paid extensions were parked for weak economics because that shelf has no billing; this is the IDE shelf that has it. Promote (open a jetbrains-plugins queue; owner action: vendor registration and bank details) if a UK sole trader can register and ≥ 3 paid plugins from vendors with ≤ 2 listings show ≥ 2,000 downloads at ≥ US$10/user/year in a ≤ 1-week niche; park if a company is required or every small-vendor paid plugin with downloads is a > 1-week build (language support, database tools). Score: evidence 1.5 (fee, payout and tax handling read from JetBrains' pages; eligibility and niche are the spike) × reach 2 (JetBrains' paid IDE user base, billing supplied) ÷ 0.5 days = 6. Done 2026-10-22 (burn-down, five relay rounds): sole trader eligible on the agreement's own words; 85 %, US$200 payout floor, VAT handled; 494 paid plugins, 83 small-vendor ones ≥ 2,000 downloads, 14 in ≤ 1-week shapes; price unreadable from the API (one first-hand €120/year), so the call is promote reshaped with the exchange's price check on 2026-10-28; parked as `jetbrains-marketplace-paid-plugins`.
items.proof: docs/exchange/spikes/jetbrains-marketplace-paid-plugins.md states whether a UK sole trader can be a paid vendor (quoting the agreement or help page), the payout and tax terms, ≥ 3 small-vendor paid plugins in one niche with downloads and price from the API, and a promote / park call

items.title: Research spike: WordPress.org plugin directory + Freemius as a freemium shelf — relay-read Freemius's pricing and docs (4.7 % revenue share plus ≈ 3.5 % gateway; is there a 2.3 % WordPress surcharge; merchant of record for VAT; US$100 payout minimum; can a UK sole trader onboard) and the WordPress.org plugin guidelines on freemium/SDK plugins, then use the keyless plugins_api (api.wordpress.org/plugins/info/1.2/?action=query_plugins&search=…) to count small-vendor plugins (author with ≤ 3 plugins) in a utility niche buildable in ≤ 1 week (UK/EU business-data blocks, compliance notices, data export and validation tools) with ≥ 1,000 active installs and a paid pro tier, and read their pro prices; write docs/exchange/spikes/wordpress-org-freemius-shelf.md with a promote / park call
items.why: new-ventures research 2026-10-22 (build; WebSearch — wordpress.org, api.wordpress.org and freemius.com do not resolve from the sandbox, hosts added). The shape: WordPress.org supplies the buyers (the directory's search and active-install counts are public across 60k+ plugins) and Freemius supplies the billing as merchant of record; neither asks for a company. Freemius's own documentation puts the fee at 4.7 % of the product price plus an average 3.5 % gateway fee, VAT and sales-tax handling included, payout at a US$100 balance; a rival merchant of record (Fungies) claims a further 2.3 % WordPress surcharge for ≈ 10.5 % all-in — the spike reads freemius.com/pricing itself. Demand is countable from the primary source: plugins_api returns active_installs, downloads, rating and author per plugin keyless, so the niche test is a number, not a guess. Risk the spike must settle: the directory lists only GPL plugins whose free tier must be useful on its own (guideline 6), so the paid tier is an upsell on an audience the directory sends — nearer audience capture than Atlassian or JetBrains, hence the lower score. Promote if a UK sole trader can onboard on Freemius and ≥ 3 small-vendor freemium plugins in a ≤ 1-week niche show ≥ 1,000 active installs with a pro tier ≥ US$29/year; park if the niche's installs sit with multi-plugin vendors or every pro tier is under US$29. items.title: Research spike: Wix App Market as a paid shelf — relay-read dev.wix.com's monetisation and payments pages (100 % of revenue in the first 12 months then 80 %; the 2.5 % transaction fee one page keeps and another says is waived; monthly payout net 30 EOM at a US$200 minimum per app) and Partner Agreement §9 (can a UK individual complete 'payout account setup'; tax forms), the Verified tier rule (60 days and 40 live Premium installs) and the App Market listing pages for a utility niche buildable in ≤ 1 week (forms and validation, business-data lookups, compliance banners): count paid apps from developers with ≤ 2 listings, their monthly prices and review counts (installs if shown); write docs/exchange/spikes/wix-app-market-paid-apps.md with a promote / park call
items.why: new-ventures research 2026-10-22 (build; WebSearch — wix.com and dev.wix.com do not resolve from the sandbox, hosts added). The developer docs make Wix the most generous shelf on paper: developers keep 100 % of sales revenue for the first 12 months and 80 % after, Wix bills the site owner and handles sales tax, and a paid app needs only a completed payout account to publish. Two facts cut the other way and set the lower score: payouts are monthly only once a single app clears US$200 of revenue share in the month (a developer feature request confirms earnings do not pool across apps), so a slow app may never pay out, and public listings show an average rating and review count but, as far as the search found, not installs — demand must be read from reviews and prices (premium apps ran US$3–24 a month in Wix's 2021 release). Promote if a UK individual can complete payout setup and ≥ 3 paid apps from small developers in a ≤ 1-week niche show ≥ 20 reviews at ≥ US$5 a month; park if a business entity is needed or the niche's paid apps have single-digit reviews. Score: evidence 1 (terms read; eligibility, installs and niche unread) × reach 2 (Wix's site owners, billing supplied) ÷ 0.5 days = 4.
